zh: 正谈到这里，七姑奶奶来招呼吃消夜。古家是很洋派的，饭厅中正摆一张桃花心木的长餐桌，六把法国宫廷式的椅子，不过坐位还是照中国规矩，拿长餐桌两端的主位当作上座，古应春夫妇分坐他的左右首作陪，弄成个反客为主的局面。消夜粥菜是火腿、皮蛋、肉松、虾子乳腐、糟油萝卜之类的酱菜，在水晶吊灯照耀之下，色彩鲜艳，颇能逗人食欲，“我想吃点酒。”胡雪岩说：“这两天筋骨有点发酸。”筋骨发酸便得喝“虎骨木瓜烧”，这是胡庆余堂所产驰名南北的药酒。胡雪岩的酒量很浅，所以七姑奶奶只替他在高脚玻璃杯中倒了半杯。
en: At this point the Seventh Lady came to call them to supper. The Gu household was decidedly Western in style. A long mahogany dining table stood in the middle of the room, surrounded by six chairs in the French court style. The seating, however, followed Chinese custom: the places at the ends of the table were treated as seats of honour. Gu and his wife sat to either side of Hu, effectively making their guest the host. With the late-night congee came ham, preserved eggs, meat floss, fermented bean curd with shrimp roe, radishes pickled in lees-flavoured sauce, and other preserved delicacies. Their bright colours under the crystal chandelier made them particularly appetizing. “I should like a little wine,” Hu said. “My muscles and joints have been aching these last two days.” Such aches called for tiger-bone and papaya liquor, a medicinal spirit made by Hu Qingyu Hall and famous throughout the country. Hu had little capacity for alcohol, so the Seventh Lady filled his stemmed glass only halfway.

zh: “七姐，”胡雪岩衔杯问道：“你啥辰光到杭州去？老太太一直在牵记你。”“我也牵记老太太。”七姑奶奶答说，“年里恐怕抽不出工夫，开了春一定去。”“喔，有件事我要跟你们商量。明年老太太六十九，后年整七十，我想趁湘阴在这里，九也要做，十也要做。”胡雪岩的门客与属下，早就在谈论，胡老太太七十整寿，要大大热闹一番。如今胡雪岩要借左宗棠两江总督的风光，明年就为胡老太太大做生日，这一点七姑奶奶倒不反对，不过俗语有“做九不做十”之说，如果“九也要做，十也要做”，就不免过分了。心里是这样想，可是不论如何，总是胡雪岩的一番孝心，不便说什么杀风景的话，只是这样答说：“九也好，十也好，只要老太太高兴就好。”
en: “Seventh Sister,” he asked, holding his glass, “when are you coming to Hangzhou? Mother keeps thinking of you.” “I think of her too. I am afraid I cannot get away before the year's end, but I shall certainly come in spring.” “There is something I want to discuss with you both. Mother will be sixty-nine next year and seventy the year after. While Xiangyin is here, I want to celebrate both birthdays—the nine and the ten.” Hu's retainers and employees had long been discussing a splendid celebration for his mother's seventieth birthday. Now he intended to use Zuo Zongtang's prestige as Governor-General of Liangjiang to give her a grand celebration a year earlier as well. The Seventh Lady did not object to celebrating next year. But custom favoured celebrating an age ending in nine rather than the following round number; doing both seemed excessive. Still, it sprang from filial affection, and she did not wish to spoil the occasion. “Nine or ten, either is good, so long as the old lady is happy.”

zh: “场面撑起来不容易，收起来也很难。”胡雪岩说，“这几年洋务发达，洋人带来的东西不少，有好的，也有坏的，学好的少，学坏的多，如果一来就坏，再学了洋人那套我们中国人不懂的花样，耍起坏来，真是让他卖到金山去当猪仔，都还不知道是怎么样到了外国的。七姐，你说可怕不可怕？“七姑奶奶不明他的用意，含含糊糊答一声：“嗯。”“前一晌有个人来跟我告帮。”胡雪岩又说：“告帮就告帮好了，这个人的说法，另有一套，他说：”胡大先生，你该当做的不做，外头就会说你的闲话，你犯不着。‘我说：“人生在世，忠孝为本，除此以外，有啥是该当做的事？我只要五伦上不亏，不管做啥，没有人好批评我。’他说，‘不然，五伦之外，有一件事是你胡大先生该当做的事。’我问：”是啥？‘你们道他怎么说？他说：“花钱。’”此人的说法是：胡雪岩以豪奢出名，所以遇到花钱的事，就是他该做的事。否则就不成其为胡雪岩了。接下来便要借五百两银子，问他作何用途，却无以为答。
en: “It is hard to establish a grand style of life, and hard to scale it back,” Hu said. “Foreign dealings have expanded these past few years, and foreigners have brought us many things, good and bad. Fewer people learn the good than the bad. If a man is bad to begin with, and then learns foreign tricks that we Chinese do not understand, there is no telling what he will do. He could sell you as a coolie to Gold Mountain before you even understood how you had reached a foreign country. Is that not frightening, Seventh Sister?” Not understanding his point, she murmured a noncommittal assent. “Someone came to me for help recently,” Hu continued. “He might simply have asked, but he had another approach. ‘Mr Hu,’ he said, ‘if you fail to do what you ought to do, people will talk. It is not worth it.’ I answered, ‘Loyalty and filial duty are the foundations of life. Beyond them, what must I do? So long as I fulfil the five human relationships, nobody has grounds to criticize my conduct.’ ‘Not so,’ he replied. ‘Beyond those five relationships, there is one thing that you, Mr Hu, ought to do.’ I asked what it was. What do you think he said? ‘Spend money.’” His argument was that Hu was famous for extravagant generosity, so any occasion requiring expenditure was properly his responsibility. Otherwise, he would cease to be Hu Xueyan. The man then asked to borrow five hundred taels, but could not say what he wanted them for.

zh: “我也晓得他要去还赌帐，如果老实跟我说，小数目也无所谓。哪晓得他说：”胡大先生，你不要问我啥用途，跟你借钱，是用不着要理由的。大家都说你一生慷慨，冤枉钱也不知道花了多少。你现在为五百两银子要问我的用途，传出去就显得你胡大先生一钿不落虚空地，不是肯花冤枉钱的人。“你们想，我要不要光火。““当然要光火。”古应春答说：“明明是要挟，意思不借给他，他就要到处去说坏话。可恶！”“可恶之极！”胡雪岩接着往下谈：“我心里在想，不借给他，用不着说，当然没有好话，借给他呢，此人说话向来刻薄，一定得便宜卖乖，说是：‘你们看，我当面骂他冤大头，他还是不敢不借给我。他就是这样子不点不亮的蜡烛脾气。’你们倒替我想想，我应该怎么办？”“叫我啊！”七姑奶奶气鼓鼓他说：“五百两银子照出，不过，他不要想用，我用他的名字捐了给善堂。”胡雪岩叹口气，“七姐，”他说：“我当时要有你这点聪明就好了。”“怎么？”古应春问：“小爷叔，你是怎么做错了呢？”
en: “I knew perfectly well that he wanted to pay gambling debts. Had he told me honestly, such a small amount would not have mattered. Instead, he said, ‘You need not ask what I want it for, Mr Hu. Nobody needs a reason to borrow from you. Everyone knows how generous you have always been and how much money you have thrown away. If word gets out that you are questioning me over five hundred taels, people will think you insist on getting value for every coin and are unwilling to waste anything.’ Tell me, should I have been angry?” “Of course,” Gu replied. “It was outright blackmail. He meant that unless you lent him the money, he would spread malicious stories. Detestable!” “Utterly detestable! I thought: if I refuse, naturally he will say nothing good of me. But if I lend it, a man with such a spiteful tongue will take the benefit and sneer at me too. He will say, ‘Look, I called him a fool to his face, and he still did not dare refuse. He is like a candle that gives no light until someone strikes a match.’ What do you think I should have done?” “If it were me,” the Seventh Lady said indignantly, “I would give the five hundred—but he would never spend it. I would donate it to a charity in his name.” Hu sighed. “If only I had possessed your wit at the time, Seventh Sister.” “Why?” Gu asked. “What did you do wrong, Little Uncle?”

zh: “我当时冷笑一声说：”不错，我胡某人一生冤枉钱不晓得花了多少，不过独独在你身上是例外。‘我身上正好有一张北京’四大恒‘的银票，数目是一千两，我说：“今天注定要破财，也说不得了。’我点根洋火，当着他的面，把那张银票饶掉了。”“他怎么样呢？气坏了？”“他倒没有气坏，说出一句话来，把我气坏了。”“他怎么说？”“他说：”胡大先生，你不要来这套骗小伢儿的把戏，你们阜康跟四大恒是同行，银票烧掉可以挂失的。‘“古应春夫妇默然。然后七姑奶奶说道：“小爷叔，你吃了哑巴亏了。”确是个哑巴亏。胡雪岩根本没有想到可以“挂失”，及至此人一说破，却又决不能去挂失，否则正好坐实了此人的说法，是“骗小伢儿的把戏”。“后来有人问我，我说有这桩事情，问我有没有挂失？我只好笑笑，答他一句：”你说呢！‘““能有人问，还是好的，至少还有个让人家看看你小爷叔态度的机会。就怕人家不问，一听说有这件事，马上就想到一定已经挂失了，问都不用问的。“古应春说：”阿七说得不错，小爷叔，你这个哑巴亏吃得很大。“
en: “I gave a cold laugh and said, ‘True, I have thrown away I do not know how much money in my life. But you are the one exception.’ I happened to have a thousand-tael note from Beijing's Four Great Heng banks in my pocket. ‘It seems I am destined to lose money today,’ I said. ‘There is no helping it.’ Then I struck a match and burned the note before his eyes.” “What did he do? Was he furious?” “He was not. He said something that made me furious.” “What?” “‘Do not try tricks for fooling children on me, Mr Hu. Fukang and the Four Great Heng are in the same business. You can report the burned note as lost.’” Gu and his wife fell silent. At last the Seventh Lady said, “Little Uncle, you suffered an injury you could not answer.” So he had. It had never occurred to Hu to register the note as lost. Once the man suggested it, however, he could no longer do so without proving the accusation that he had merely staged a children's trick. “Later, when people asked, I admitted the incident. If they asked whether I had reported the loss, I could only smile and say, ‘What do you think?’” “It is better when people ask,” Gu observed. “At least they can see your manner for themselves. The danger is those who hear the story and immediately assume you must have reported it, without thinking a question necessary. A'qi is right. You suffered badly from this.”

zh: “吃了亏要学乖。”胡雪岩接口说道：“我后来想想，这位仁兄的确是有道理，花钱的事，就是我该当做的事，根本就不应去问他的用途。如果说我花得冤枉了，那么我挣来的钱呢？在我这面说，挣钱靠眼光、靠手腕、靠精神力气，不过我也要想想亏本的人，他那面蚀本蚀得冤枉，我这面挣的就是冤枉钱。”“小爷叔的论调，越来越玄妙了。”古应春笑道：“挣钱也有冤枉的？”“挣了钱不会用，挣的就是冤枉钱。”胡雪岩问道：“淮扬一带有种‘磐响钱’，你们有没有听说过？”古应春初闻此“磐响钱”三字，七姑奶奶倒听说过，有那一班铢锱必较，积资千万，而恶衣恶食，一钱如命的富商，偏偏生个败家子，无奈做老子的钱管得紧，就只好到处借债了，利息当然比向“老西儿”借印子钱还要凶，却有一样好处，在败家子还不起钱的时候，决不会来催讨。“那么要到什么时候还呢？”七姑奶奶自问自答地为古应春解释：“要到他老子死的那天。人一咽气，头一件事是请个和尚来念‘倒头经，，和尚手里的磐一响，债主就上门了，所以叫做磐响钱。”“与其不孝子孙来花，不如自己花，自我得之，自我失之，本来也无所谓。不过，小爷叔，你说花钱的事，就是该当你做的事，这话，”古应春很含蓄他说：“只怕也还有斟酌的余地。”
en: “One must learn from a loss,” Hu replied. “Afterwards I thought the fellow did have a point. Spending money is what I ought to do. I should never have asked his purpose. If my spending is wasteful, what about the money I earn? From my side, I earn through judgment, skill, energy, and effort. But I ought to consider the man who loses. If he regards his loss as money thrown away, then what I gain is that same thrown-away money.” “Your reasoning grows more mysterious all the time,” Gu said with a laugh. “Can earning money be a waste too?” “If you do not know how to use it, earning it is a waste. Have you heard of the ‘death-bell loans’ around Huai'an and Yangzhou?” Gu had never heard the expression, but the Seventh Lady knew it. Some rich merchants counted every penny, accumulated enormous fortunes, and yet ate and dressed miserably, clinging to each coin as though it were life itself. Unfortunately, they sometimes produced wastrel sons. With their fathers keeping such a tight grip on the purse, the sons borrowed wherever they could. Interest was even more savage than on the instalment loans of the Shanxi moneylenders. But there was one advantage: if the prodigal could not pay, the creditors would never press him. “When, then, did repayment fall due?” the Seventh Lady explained to Gu. “On the day his father died. As soon as the old man stopped breathing, the first thing was to summon a monk to chant the prayers at the deathbed. The moment the monk struck his chime, the creditors came to the door. That is why they were called death-bell loans.” “Better spend it oneself than leave it for unfilial descendants,” Gu said. “What one has gained oneself, one may lose oneself; that need not matter. But the proposition that every expense is your duty, Little Uncle—perhaps that still deserves some consideration.”

zh: “我想过好几遍了，既然人家叫我‘财神’，我就是应该散财的，不然就有烦恼。”胡雪岩急转直下地回入本题，“譬如说明年老太太六十九，我一定要做。不做，忌我的人就有话说了，怎么说呢？说胡某人一向好面子，如今两江总督是左大人，正好借他的威风来耍一耍排场，不做不是他不想做，是左大人对他不比从前了，胡老太太做生日，礼是当然要送的，不过普普通通一份寿礼，想要如何替做面子，是不会有的事。倒不如自己识相为妙。七姐，你说，如果我不做，是不是会有这种情形。”七姑奶奶不能不承认，却换了一种说法：“做九原是好做的。”“明年做了九，后年还要做。”胡雪岩又说：“如果不做，又有人说闲话了，说胡老太太做七十岁是早已定规了的。只为想借左大人招摇，所以提前一年。做过了也就算了，他这两年的境况不比从前，能省就省了。七姐，你要晓得，这比明年不做还要坏！”“为什么呢？”“这点你还不明白？”古应春接口：“这句话一传开来，阜康的存款就要打折扣了。”“岂止打折扣？”胡雪岩掉了句文：“牵一发而动全身，马上就是一个大风浪。”
en: “I have thought it over repeatedly. Since people call me the God of Wealth, I ought to distribute wealth. Otherwise I invite trouble.” Hu abruptly returned to his original subject. “Take Mother's sixty-ninth birthday next year. I must celebrate it. If I do not, those who envy me will have something to say. They will say I have always loved appearances, and that with His Excellency Zuo now Governor-General of Liangjiang, I ought to be eager to borrow his prestige for a grand display. If I refrain, it cannot be because I do not want one; it must be because Zuo no longer treats me as before. Of course he would send Mother a birthday present, but only an ordinary one. He would do nothing special to enhance the occasion. Better for me, then, to recognize my position and keep quiet. Seventh Sister, would people not say that if I held no celebration?” She could not deny it, but answered differently. “There is nothing wrong with celebrating the sixty-ninth.” “And after celebrating it next year, I must celebrate again the year after. Otherwise people will say Mother's seventieth had long been planned, but I brought it forward a year to exploit Zuo's prestige. Having held it once, I let it suffice, because my circumstances have declined and I must economize where I can. You must understand, Seventh Sister, that this would be worse than not celebrating next year.” “Why?” “Do you not see?” Gu intervened. “Once that rumour spreads, Fukang's deposits will shrink.” “Shrink is hardly the word!” Hu quoted a literary saying: “Pull one hair and the whole body moves. A major storm would break immediately.”

zh: 七姑奶奶无法想象，会是怎佯的一种“大风浪”？只是看他脸上有难得一见的警惕之色，忍不住将她藏之心中已久的一句话说了出来。“小爷叔，我也要劝你，好收好了。不过，我这句话，跟老太太说的。意思稍为有点不同，老太太是说排场能收则收。不必再摆开来，我说的收一收是能不做的生意不做，该做的生意要好好儿做。“此言一出，首先古应春觉得十分刺耳，不免责备：“你这话是怎么说的？小爷叔做生意，还要你来批评？““应春！”胡雪岩伸手按着他摆在桌上的手，拦住他的话说：“现在肯同我说真话的，只有七姐了。我要听！”说着还重重地点一点头。古应春原是觉得胡雪岩的性情，跟以前不大一样了，伯七姑奶奶言语过于率直，惹他心中不快，即或不言，总是件扫兴的事。即然他乐闻逆耳之言，他当然没有再阻挠的必要，不过仍旧向妻子抛了个眼色，示意她措词要婉转。“有些话我摆在肚皮里好久了，想说没有机会。即然小爷叔要听，我就实话直说了，得罪人我也不怕，只要小爷叔有一句两句听进去，就算人家记我的恨，我也是犯得着的。”
en: The Seventh Lady could not picture precisely what such a storm would mean. But seeing an unusually apprehensive expression on his face, she could not keep back something she had long wished to say. “Little Uncle, I too must advise you to draw things in. My meaning differs a little from your mother's. She says you should reduce the display where possible, instead of expanding it further. I mean that you should stop businesses you need not conduct, and manage properly those you ought to keep.” Gu was the first to find this painfully offensive. “What do you mean? Does Little Uncle need you to criticize his business?” “Yingchun!” Hu laid a hand over Gu's on the table to stop him. “Seventh Sister is the only person still willing to tell me the truth. I want to hear it.” He nodded emphatically. Gu had noticed that Hu's temperament was no longer quite what it had been. He feared his wife's bluntness would offend him; even if Hu said nothing, the evening would be spoiled. Since Hu welcomed unwelcome truths, Gu had no reason to obstruct her, although he still gave her a glance urging tact. “I have kept some things inside for a long time, without an opportunity to say them,” she began. “Since you wish to listen, I shall speak plainly. I am not afraid of offending people. If even one or two of my remarks reach you, their resentment will be worth it.”

zh: 由这一段开场白，胡雪岩便知她要批评他所用的人。对这一点，他很在意，也很自负，他认为他之有今日立下这番乾嘉年间，扬州盐商全盛时期都及不上的局面，得力于他能识人，更能用人，这当然要明查暗访，才能知道一个人的长处何在，毛病在哪里。不过，他听人月旦人物，胸中却自有丘壑，首先要看批评人的人，自己有没有可批评之处，然后才来衡量那些批评，哪一句是可以听的，哪一句是对方希望他能听的。七姑奶奶是极少数他认为应该佩服的人之一，她对人的批评，不但要听，而且唯恐她言之不尽，因而觉得有鼓励她的必要。“七姐，没有人会记你的恨，因为没有人会晓得你同我说的话。你有见到的地方，尽管说，就是我有错处，你亦不必客气，你说了实话，我只有感激，决不会怪你。”有这样诚恳的表示，反使得七姑奶奶觉得光是批评某些人，犹不足以尽其忠悃，要批评就要从根本上去批评毛病的由来。
en: From this introduction Hu knew she meant to criticize the people he employed. This was a matter in which he took great interest and pride. He believed that his achievement—an establishment surpassing even the Yangzhou salt merchants at their height in the Qianlong and Jiaqing reigns—rested on his ability both to judge people and to use them. Naturally, discovering a person's strengths and faults required open observation and discreet inquiry. Yet when listening to judgments of character, he followed principles of his own. First he examined the critic: was that person open to criticism? Only then did he weigh the remarks, distinguishing what he ought to hear from what the speaker merely wanted him to believe. The Seventh Lady was among the very few people he felt he should admire. He wanted not only to hear her judgments but to ensure that she left nothing unsaid. He therefore encouraged her. “Nobody will resent you, Seventh Sister, because nobody will know what you tell me. Say whatever you have observed. Even if I am at fault, do not spare me. I shall be grateful for the truth, never angry with you.” His sincerity made her feel that criticizing particular employees would not adequately express her loyalty. She must go deeper, to the source of the faults.

zh: “小爷叔，说实话，跟前个十来年比起来，我对你的敬重打折扣了。不过小爷叔，对你的关心，是有增无减。思前想后，有时候为你想得一夜困不着。”这话说得胡雪岩耸然动容，“七姐，”他说：“我们是患难之交，我最佩服你是女中丈夫。我自己也知道，做人处世，没有十几年前那样，处处为人着想，不过，总还不算对不起人。场面虽然扯得大，用的人是得力的，里里外外都绷得牢，不晓得七姐是为啥为我愁得一夜困不着。”“我愁的是树大招风。小爷叔，你是丈八灯台，多少人沾你的光，照出一条路来，走得又快又稳，可惜你照不见自己。”“丈八灯台”这句俗语，是如此用法，胡雪岩觉得格外贴切，因而也就更重视她的下文了。“七姐，亏得还有你看得清楚。今天没有外人，请你老实说，我有哪些毛病要改？”七姑奶奶沉吟不语。她本想着：你认为你用的人都得力，里外部能绷得住，这一点就要改，不过这好象一概抹煞，会惹胡雪岩起反感，而况事实上也有困难，如果他这样说一句：照你说起来，我用的人通通要换过，请问，一时三刻哪里去找这么多人？找来的人是不是个个靠得住。这就无辞以答了。古应春多少看出她的心思，怕她说得过分徒乱人意，无稗实际，便暗示她说：“阿七，你谈一两件小事，小爷叔心里自然有数。”“好！”七姑奶奶接受了这个建议，略想一想说道：“小爷叔，我讲两件你自己不知道，人家替你得罪了人，都记在你帐上的事。”
en: “To be honest, Little Uncle, I respect you less than I did ten or more years ago. But my concern for you has increased, not diminished. Sometimes I think about your affairs until I cannot sleep all night.” Hu was visibly shaken. “We are friends who have endured hardship together, Seventh Sister. What I most admire is your courage and integrity. I know I am not as considerate of others in everything as I was ten or more years ago. Still, I have not treated people badly. My establishment is large, but the people I employ are capable, and everything is held firmly together, inside and out. I do not understand what worries you so much that you cannot sleep.” “What worries me is that a great tree catches the wind. You are a towering lampstand, Little Uncle. So many people borrow your light to find their way and move ahead quickly and safely. Yet you cannot illuminate yourself.” Hu found this use of the familiar saying particularly apt, and listened still more attentively. “Fortunately, you can see clearly. There are no outsiders here today. Tell me honestly: what faults must I change?” She hesitated. Her first thought was that his very belief in the competence of all his people and the security of his affairs needed changing. But that sounded like a wholesale condemnation and might provoke resistance. There was a practical difficulty too. If he asked whether he must replace everyone, where so many replacements could be found at once, and whether they would all be trustworthy, she could not answer. Gu partly understood her hesitation. Fearing that excessive criticism would merely unsettle Hu without practical benefit, he suggested, “A'qi, describe one or two small incidents. Little Uncle will draw his own conclusions.” “Very well.” She thought briefly. “I shall tell you of two occasions when others offended people on your behalf, without your knowledge, and the blame was entered against your name.”

zh: 第一件花园落成以后，胡雪岩对其中的假山不满意，决心改造。请了几个专工此道的人来看，画了图样，亦不见得有何出色之处，最后打听到京中有个大名家，姓应单名一个崇字，河南人，咸丰初年是怡亲王载垣门下的清客。辛酉政变，载垣家破人亡，应崇眼看起高楼，眼看他楼坍了，感慨甚深，因而遁人西山，闭门课子，不闻外事。好在当年载垣炙手可热时，应崇曾获厚赠，粗茶淡饭的生计，维持个几年，还不至于拮据。这应崇本来不想出山，经不起胡雪岩卑词厚币，加以派去延请的刘不才，能言善道，终于将他请到了杭州。实地看了已造好的假山，又看了好些绘而未用的图样，应崇觉得也不算太坏，只需修改，不必重造。但胡雪岩不以为然，坚持全盘更新。应崇心想，这是钱太多的缘故，不过，这话不便说破，交浅言深，会使得胡雪岩误会他胸中本无丘壑，所以才敢拆了重造。
en: The first concerned Hu's garden. After it was completed, he disliked the rockery and decided to rebuild it. Several specialists inspected it and produced plans, but none impressed him. Eventually he heard of an eminent master in Beijing, Ying Chong, a native of Henan. Early in the Xianfeng reign, Ying had been a retainer of Prince Yi, Zaiyuan. The Xinyou coup destroyed Zaiyuan's household and cost him his life. Having watched the great mansion rise and then collapse, Ying was deeply affected. He withdrew to the Western Hills, shut his door, taught his children, and ignored outside affairs. Generous gifts received during Zaiyuan's ascendancy meant that a few years of simple living would not leave him destitute. He had no wish to return to worldly employment. But Hu's humble entreaties and generous payment, reinforced by the persuasive Liu Bucai, who had been sent to invite him, eventually brought him to Hangzhou. Having inspected the existing rockery and several unused designs, Ying thought them reasonably good. Alteration would suffice; complete rebuilding was unnecessary. Hu disagreed and insisted on starting afresh. Ying privately thought this the consequence of having too much money. Yet he could not say so: such frankness before their acquaintance had deepened might lead Hu to think he lacked the imaginative resources to dare demolish and rebuild it.

zh: 也就是这好强争胜的一念，应崇关起门来，一个月不下楼，画成了一幅草图，却还不肯出以示人，每天在六桥三竺之间，策杖徜徉，或者深入南北高峰，探幽搜奇，回来挑灯展图，细细修改。到得三个月后，终于杀青了。这一套图一共十七张，一幅总图、十六幅分图，奇岩怪壑，百折干回，方丈之地，以小见大，令人拍案叫绝。胡雪岩大喜过望，设盛筵款待，当面约请监工，应崇也答应了。造假山当然要选奇石。杭州是南宋的都城，名园甚多，也有废弃了的，应崇一一看过。却都不甚当意。这天到了贡院西桥，一处废园，据说原是严嵩的干儿子赵文华的祠堂，其中有块卧倒在地的石头，却大有可观。论百之美，有个三字诀，叫做“瘦、皱、透”，应崇看这块石头虽一半埋在土中，但露出地面的部分，足以当此三字，判断另一半亦夏如是。
en: Stung by the desire to prove himself, Ying shut himself away and did not come downstairs for a month, until he had completed a preliminary design. Even then he would not show it. Each day he walked with his staff among the Six Bridges and Three Tianzhu Temples, or explored the Northern and Southern Peaks in search of secluded and remarkable scenery. At night he spread out the plans by lamplight and revised them carefully. After three months the work was finally complete: seventeen drawings, one general plan and sixteen detailed sheets. Strange rocks, unusual ravines, and countless winding turns made a small space suggest an immense landscape. The result inspired delighted admiration. Overjoyed, Hu entertained him at a lavish banquet and asked him to supervise construction. Ying agreed. A rockery required exceptional stones. Hangzhou, the Southern Song capital, contained many famous gardens, including abandoned ones. Ying inspected them all, without finding much to satisfy him. One day he came to a ruined garden by Gongyuan West Bridge, said to have been the ancestral shrine of Zhao Wenhua, Yan Song's adopted son. A stone lying on its side there caught his attention. Three qualities defined a fine ornamental rock: slenderness, wrinkled texture, and openings through its body. Although half buried, the exposed portion possessed all three, and Ying judged that the hidden half must be equally fine.

zh: 正在反复观赏之时，只见有个须眉全白老者，短衣草鞋，手里捏一支湘妃竹的旱烟袋，意态消闲地踱了过来。应崇看他打扮不似缙绅先生，那气度却似退归林下的大老，顿时肃然起敬地问讯。“老先生尊姓？”“不敢当。我姓赵。足下贵姓？”“敝姓应。”应崇问道：“请问赵老先生，这废园可有人管？”“怎么没有？我就是。”“喔！失敬，失敬。”应崇连连拱手。赵老者一面擎着旱烟袋还礼，一面问道：“足下要找管园的，有何见教。”“想请教请教这块石头。”赵老者点点头，将应崇自上而下端详了一番问道：“足下想来亦有米颠之癖。既承下问，不敢不告。提起这块石头，大有来历，原是从大梁艮岳运来的。”原来是宋徽宗艮岳的旧物，千里迢迢，从开封运来，亘历六七百年之久，名贵可知……“足下恐怕还不知道这块石头真正的妙处”赵老者回头喊道：“小四儿，拿根浪竿来！”晾衣服用的竹竿，杭州叫做“浪竿”。小四儿知道要“浪竿”作何用途，取了来一言不发，从石头的一端伸进竹竿去。这时应崇才发现石头中间有个碗大的孔，贯通两头，竹竿很容易地从另一面冒出头来。“这才是真正的‘一线天’。”应崇很快地想到这块石头叠在假山上，到得正午，阳光直射入山洞，圆圆的一道光柱，岂非很别致的一景。
en: As he examined it from every angle, an old man whose beard and eyebrows were completely white strolled over. He wore a short jacket and straw sandals and carried a spotted-bamboo pipe. His clothes were not those of a gentleman, but his bearing suggested a great official retired into seclusion. Ying greeted him respectfully. “May I ask your surname, sir?” “You are too kind. Zhao. And yours?” “Ying. Is anyone responsible for this abandoned garden, Mr Zhao?” “Certainly. I am.” “Ah! Forgive my ignorance.” Ying repeatedly clasped his hands in greeting. Returning the salute with his pipe raised, Zhao asked why he wanted the keeper. “I hoped to ask about this stone.” Zhao nodded, looked him over, and said, “You seem to share Mi the Eccentric's passion. Since you ask, I must tell you. The stone has a distinguished history: it came from Genyue in Daliang.” So it had belonged to Emperor Huizong's Genyue garden, carried all the way from Kaifeng six or seven centuries earlier. Its rarity was obvious. “Perhaps you have not yet discovered its finest feature.” Zhao turned and called, “Little Fourth, bring a drying pole!” In Hangzhou, a bamboo pole for hanging clothes was called a langgan. Little Fourth knew what it was wanted for. Without a word he inserted it into one end of the stone. Only then did Ying notice a bowl-sized hole running right through it. The pole easily emerged at the other end. “A true thread of sky!” Ying immediately imagined the stone incorporated into the rockery, with the midday sun shining through it into a cavern as a round shaft of light. What an exquisite scene that would make.

zh: “赵老，”应崇率直问道：“这块石头能不能割爱？”赵老者又细看了几眼，开口问道：“足下是自己起造园林，还是为人物色材料。”“实不相瞒，我是应胡财神之邀，替他来改造花园。得此奇石，我的图样又要修改了。”“原来是他！”赵老者摇摇头说：“我不造这个孽。”应崇愕然，“赵老，”他问：“这话怎么说？”“说起来，这位胡大先生倒是值得佩服的，好事也做得不少。可惜，这几年来骄奢淫逸，大改本性，都是他手下那班卑鄙小人奉承得他不知道天高地厚。从来勤俭兴家，骄奢必败。只看这块石头，当年道君皇帝，如果不是要起艮岳，弄出什么‘花石纲’，金兵哪里到得了汴梁？足下既以此为业，想来平生也替达官贵人造过不少花园，不知道这几家的主人，有哪几家是有贤子孙的？至于这位胡大先生，尾大不掉，真是他的好朋友要劝劝他，趁早收山，倘或依旧撺掇他挥霍无度，迟早有受良心责备之一日。“
en: “Mr Zhao,” he asked directly, “could you bear to part with it?” Zhao studied him again. “Are you building a garden for yourself, or finding materials for someone else?” “To be frank, the God of Wealth, Hu, invited me to remodel his garden. If I obtain this remarkable stone, I shall have to revise my design again.” “So it is for him!” Zhao shook his head. “I will not commit that sin.” Ying was astonished. “What do you mean?” “Mr Hu is admirable in many ways and has done a great deal of good. Unfortunately, these past few years he has become proud, extravagant, indulgent, and idle, quite changing his nature. Those despicable flatterers under him have made him forget all limits. Diligence and thrift build a household; pride and extravagance ruin it. Consider this very stone. Had Emperor Huizong not built Genyue and imposed his flower-and-rock transport levies, how could the Jin armies have reached Bianliang? Since garden building is your profession, you must have worked for many wealthy and powerful families. How many of their owners have worthy descendants? As for Mr Hu, his establishment has grown too large to control. A true friend would urge him to withdraw while there is time. Anyone who continues encouraging his reckless expenditure will sooner or later feel the reproach of conscience.”

zh: 这番侃侃而谈，使得应崇汗流侠背，深悔出山之非计。但事已如此，总不能说退还聘金，收回图样，只好托词家乡有急事，坚辞监工的职务。胡雪岩再三挽留留不住，只好请他荐贤自代。应崇却不过情，而且毕竟是一番心血所寄，也怕为俗手埋没，看胡家的清客中，有个名叫曾笑苏的，对此道不算外行，有时谈起来颇有创见，因而说了句，“曾笑苏堪当此任。”胡雪岩用人，一定要先摸清此人的本事，随即将曾笑苏请了来，当着应崇的面，要他细看图样，然后问道：“照应先生的图样，不晓得要多少日子，才能完工？”“这，”曾笑苏笑道：“当着大行家在这里，哪有我置喙的余地。”“不敢，不敢！”应崇接口，同时抛了个眼色给他：“笑苏兄，请你估计。”曾笑苏会意，监工这个有油水的好差使，多半可以捞得到手了，当下聚精会神地盘算了好一会，方始问道：“大先生想多少日子完工？”
en: The speech left Ying sweating and deeply regretting his decision to emerge from retirement. Yet matters had gone too far for him to return his fee and withdraw his plans. He could only plead urgent business at home and firmly decline the supervision. Unable to detain him despite repeated entreaties, Hu asked him to recommend a replacement. Ying found it hard to refuse. The design also embodied much effort, and he feared seeing it ruined by an incompetent hand. Among Hu's retainers was Zeng Xiaosu, who knew something of the art and occasionally offered original ideas in conversation. Ying therefore said that Zeng could undertake the task. Hu always wanted to establish a man's abilities before employing him. He summoned Zeng, had him examine the drawings in Ying's presence, and asked how long construction would take. “With a great master here,” Zeng said, smiling, “how could I venture an opinion?” “Not at all!” Ying interjected, giving him a meaningful glance. “Please make an estimate, Brother Xiaosu.” Zeng understood that this profitable assignment was probably within reach. He concentrated on calculations for a while, then asked, “When would you like it finished, sir?”

zh: “五十天如何？”“五十天就得要用一百二十个人。”曾笑苏屈着手指计算，“照图施工，四处山洞，每洞工匠二十名，下余四十名，专运石料。舂浆五天，施工二十天，预备改作十天，结顶十天。如果一切顺利，四十五天可以完工。大先生要大宴宾客，日子挑在五十天以后好了。”胡雪岩不置可否，转脸问道：“应先生看怎么样？”“算得很精明。不过稍微紧了一点，施工的时候，稍一放松，五十天就不够用了。”“原有五天的余裕打在里面。”曾笑苏答说：“应先生，你老有所不知，淌或是在别处施工，也许石料不齐。人手不足，我不敢说哪天一定可以完工，在我们胡大先生府上，要人有人、要钱有钱、要料有料，五十天完工，是有把握的。”“说得是。”有应崇这句话，就象朝廷逢到子午卯西大比之年，放各省乡试主考，先钦派两榜出身的大员，将够资梧派充考官的京官，集合起来，考上一考，合格了方能放出去当正副主考那样，曾笑苏能充任监工之职，已由应崇认可，胡雪岩自是信任不疑。
en: “How about fifty days?” “Fifty days would require one hundred and twenty workers.” Zeng counted on his fingers. “There are four grottoes in the design: twenty craftsmen for each, leaving forty men to transport stone. Five days to pound the mortar, twenty for construction, ten allowed for alterations, and ten to complete the tops. If everything goes smoothly, forty-five days will suffice. You may arrange your grand banquet for fifty days from the start.” Hu neither agreed nor disagreed, but turned to Ying. “What do you think?” “The calculation is intelligent, but rather tight. Any slackening during construction, and fifty days will be insufficient.” “I have allowed five days' margin,” Zeng replied. “You may not realize, sir, that elsewhere I might hesitate to promise a fixed date because materials or labour could be short. Here, whatever workers, money, or materials are needed can be supplied. I am confident of finishing in fifty days.” “That is true.” Ying's approval was like the certification of examination officials. In the provincial examination years corresponding to Zi, Wu, Mao, and You, the court first appointed senior officials who had passed both higher examinations to test the eligible capital officials; only those who passed could be sent out as chief and deputy examiners. Ying had similarly certified Zeng's competence to supervise, and Hu consequently trusted him without reservation.

zh: 于是择吉开工，一百二十名工匠，在早经将原有假山拆掉的空地上，分做十二圈，开始舂浆。事先有总管胡云福关照：“舂浆不能出声，老太太讨厌那种声音。”原来其中有个讲究。所谓舂浆的浆，杭州人称之为“袅浆”，专有一种树叶子，用水一泡，稠稠地象妇女梳头用的刨花水，然后用石灰、黄泥掺合，加入这种稠汁，就可以开始舂了。舂浆的法子是，几个人绕着石灰、黄泥围成一圈，每人手里一把齐腰的丁字锤，锤身是饭碗粗的一根栗木桩，桩底镶半圆形的铁锤，柱顶有条两尺长镶得很牢固的横木，以便把握。到得围拢站齐，为头的一声讯号，往后退步，腰身挺起，顺势将丁字锤往上一翻，翻到朝天往下落，同时进步弯腰，锤头重重舂在石灰、黄泥上。另有人不断地用木勺舀着稠汁往上浇。起始是白灰、黄泥的然可见，后来浑然融合，舂得愈久，韧性愈佳。杭州人修造坟墓，棺木四周，必实以袅浆，干燥以后，坚硬异常，真正是“刀枪不入”，杭州盗墓之风不炽，即因得力于袅浆。至于有那要迁葬的，另有一个破袅浆之法，法于是打开坟头，遍浇烈性烧酒，用火点燃，等酒尽火熄，泥质发脆，自能下锄。
en: An auspicious day was chosen, and work began. The old rockery had already been demolished. On the cleared ground, one hundred and twenty craftsmen formed twelve circles and began pounding mortar. The steward, Hu Yunfu, had instructed them beforehand: “No calling out while you pound. The old lady dislikes the noise.” There was a special reason for this. The mortar, known in Hangzhou as niaojiang, used a particular kind of leaf which, soaked in water, produced a thick liquid resembling the wood-shaving infusion women used to dress their hair. This was added to lime and yellow clay before pounding. Several men stood in a circle around the mixture, each holding a waist-high T-shaped rammer. Its shaft was a piece of chestnut wood as thick as a rice bowl, with a rounded iron head at the bottom and a firmly fitted crosspiece two chi long at the top. At the leader's signal, the men stepped back, straightened, and swung their rammers upward. As the tools descended, they stepped forward and bent, driving the heads heavily into the lime and clay. Another worker continuously ladled on the thick leaf infusion. At first, white lime and yellow clay remained distinct; gradually they blended, and the longer the pounding continued, the tougher the mixture became. In Hangzhou, tomb builders packed it around coffins. Once dry, it became extraordinarily hard, virtually impervious to blades and weapons. The rarity of grave robbery there was attributed to this mortar. When a burial had to be moved, there was a separate method for breaking it: the tomb was opened, strong liquor poured over the mortar and ignited, and, after the liquor and flames were exhausted, the material became brittle enough to work with a hoe.

zh: 从前明太祖造南京城，责成元末巨富沈万三施工，城墙用巨石堆砌，接缝用糯米熬浆粘合，所以能历数百年不坏。袅浆居然亦有此功用，最要紧的是，舂得匀、舂得久，所以为头的讯号，关系不浅，而讯号无非“邪许”之声，从宣泄劳苦的“力笨之歌”中，音节上自然有指挥下锤轻重徐疾，计算锤数，以及移动步伐“尺寸”的作用在内，舂袅浆的人，一面舂。一面慢慢向右转，为的是求均匀，同时亦为计算工夫的一种方法，大致总要转到十二至十六圈，那袅浆的功用，才能发挥到顶点。除了修造坟墓以外，袅浆另外的用途，就是起造假山，石料与石料的接台，非用袅浆，不能坚固。但这一有特殊音节的“邪许”之声，春秋每闻于定山，自然而然地使人意识到，附近又有一座新坟在造。胡老太太年纪大了，恶闻此声，所以由胡云福交代下来，不准出声。这一来便如军队失去号令，自然混乱不齐，手脚慢了。曾笑苏求功心切，不免责骂叱喝，工匠敢怒不敢言，到得散工出门，议论纷纷，不说曾笑苏不体恤人，却说胡家刻薄。
en: When the Ming founder built Nanjing's walls, he had charged Shen Wansan, the immensely wealthy man of the late Yuan, with construction. Massive stones were joined with boiled glutinous-rice paste, enabling the walls to endure for centuries. Niaojiang could perform a similar function. What mattered most was prolonged, even pounding, making the leader's signals indispensable. These were the familiar heave-ho cries of labour. Their rhythm, while expressing the workers' exertion, naturally directed the force and speed of each stroke, counted the blows, and regulated the length of their steps. As they worked, the men slowly moved round to their right, both to ensure even mixing and to measure the labour performed. Usually twelve to sixteen circuits were needed to bring the mortar to its full strength. Besides tomb building, it was used in rockeries, where only this material could firmly join the stones. But the distinctive pounding chant was often heard around burial grounds in spring and autumn, inevitably suggesting that another grave was being built nearby. Hu's elderly mother disliked hearing it; hence Hu Yunfu's order for silence. Without the chant, the workers were like soldiers deprived of commands. Their movements became disordered and slow. Eager to succeed, Zeng scolded and shouted at them. They dared not voice their anger at work, but talked bitterly as they left. Their complaint was not that Zeng lacked consideration, but that the Hu household was cruel.

zh: 刻薄之事，不是没有，只是胡雪岩根本不知。从来大户人家有所兴作，包工或者工头，总难免偷工减料。起造假山，料无可减，工却可偷，只以曾笑苏颇为精明，不敢虚报人数，只以学徒下手混充熟练的工匠，头两天还好，到第三天情形就不对了，曾笑苏挖空心思，走了个规矩，工钱不许先支，当日发给。散工时，园门口置特制的八尺多高条凳一张，每班十二人，上置十二份工钱，各人自取，不得接手代递，手不够长拿不到的，就算白做。不但未成年的学徒，只好眼泪汪汪，空手出门，就是身矮的，也是徒呼奈何。曾笑苏还得意洋洋地表功，道是“身长力不亏。矮子纵有气力也有限，试问堆假山没有力气，有何用处？这是存优汰劣的不二法门”。可是外头的舆论就不堪闻问了，传来传去，说是胡雪岩伏势欺人，叫人做了工，不发工钱。有人不信，说，：胡大先生做好事出名的，哪里会有这样刻薄“，无奈人证俱在，想替他说好话的人，也开不得口了。
en: Cruelty was indeed occurring, though Hu knew nothing of it. Whenever a great household undertook construction, contractors or foremen were apt to skimp on labour or materials. In building a rockery there was little scope to economize on the stone, but labour could be cheated. Because Zeng was shrewd, the contractors dared not inflate the headcount; instead they passed apprentices and assistants off as skilled craftsmen. The first two days went well, but by the third something was wrong. Racking his brains, Zeng devised a rule: no wages could be drawn in advance, and payment would be made at the end of each day. A specially built long bench more than eight chi high stood by the garden gate. For each group of twelve men, twelve wage packets were placed on it. Everyone had to reach for his own; nobody could pass a packet to someone else. Anyone whose arm did not reach received nothing for his day's work. Young apprentices left empty-handed and tearful, but short adults were equally helpless. Zeng proudly claimed credit for the arrangement: tall men had ample strength, he said, while even a strong short man had limited power. What use was a rockery builder without strength? This was the surest means of retaining the able and eliminating the unfit. Public opinion, however, became appalling. As the story spread, it was said that Hu abused his power by making men work without paying them. Some protested that a man famous for charity could never be so harsh. But witnesses were available, and even those wishing to defend him were silenced.

zh: 还有件事，更为荒唐。一年胡雪岩为亡父冥寿作佛事，时逢初冬，施衣施食，只要自己舍得下脸的，都可以排队来领，每人蓝市棉袄一件，饭碗大的白面馒头四个。棉袄、馒头都经胡雪岩自己看过，尝过，毫不马虎。这场好事，应该做得很好，不迫有人咬牙切齿在痛骂。说来说去，还是胡雪岩用人不当，主事的胆大妄为。原来有那贪小的，排了一次队，第二次再来，多领一份。这往宽处说，他也是花了工夫气力，多换得一份施舍，不算白捡便宜，就算从严，训斥几句，亦就至矣尽矣，谁知主事者别出心裁，等人头一次来领了棉袄、馒头，到出口处有一班，“待沼”在等着，剃头匠别称“待沼”。每人一把剃刀，头发剃去一块，作为已领施舍的记号，倘或不愿，除非不领。“小爷叔，”七姑奶奶谈到这件事，犹有余愤，“你倒想想，有的天不亮去排队，轮到日中才轮到，料不到有这么一个规矩，要不领呢，白吃一场辛苦，于心不甘，要领呢，头发缺一块，挂了块穿舍衣的招牌在那里，真叫进退两难，有个不咬牙切齿的吗？”
en: Another incident was still more outrageous. One year, early in winter, Hu held Buddhist rites for his late father's posthumous birthday and distributed food and clothing. Anyone willing to endure the embarrassment of accepting charity could queue for a blue cotton padded jacket and four white-flour steamed buns, each as large as a rice bowl. Hu had personally inspected the jackets and tasted the buns, taking every care. The charitable event should have gone well. Instead, people cursed him through clenched teeth. Again, the fault lay in his choice of subordinates and their reckless conduct. Some recipients, wanting a little extra, joined the queue a second time for another portion. A generous view would recognize that they had spent further time and effort to obtain it, rather than gained something for nothing. Even a strict response need have gone no further than a reprimand. But the organizers devised a novel system. After receiving a jacket and buns, each person encountered a group of daizhao, as barbers were also called, waiting at the exit with a razor in each man’s hand. A patch of hair was shaved off as proof that charity had already been received. Anyone unwilling to submit had to forgo the gifts. “Little Uncle,” the Seventh Lady said, still angry at the recollection, “imagine someone queuing before dawn and waiting until noon, without knowing of this rule. To refuse would mean all that hardship for nothing. To accept would leave a bald patch advertising that he wore charity clothes. What a choice! How could people help feeling bitter?”

zh: 这几句话说得胡雪岩脸上红一阵、青一阵，深秋天气，背上却湿漉漉地冒汗，“七姐，”他说：“你说的情形，我一点都不知道。我回去要查，查出来我要狗血喷头，骂他一顿。”“你也不必去查。这个人已经不在小爷叔你那里了，我才说的。”“这样说，还有这样子的人在那里？”七姑奶奶默然，也就是默认，古应春觉得话既说到如此，就索性再劝一劝他。古应春追随胡雪岩多年，当初创业维艰的经过大多熟悉，所以劝他的话不但很多，而且也很深刻，“小爷叔，”他说：“你的事业当中，典当在你看，完全是为了方便穷人，不想赚钱。话是这样说，天下哪有不赚钱的典当？不过，因为你有这番意思在那里，明明应该赚的也不赚了、小爷叔，这一层，不知道你想过没有？““我想过。我同他们说：钱庄是有钱人的当铺，当铺是穷人的钱庄，有钱的人，我来对付，他‘当信用’、‘当交情’，能不能当，能当多少，多大致有数。穷人太多，我照顾不到，都托你们了，大家要凭天良。我想，那班‘徽州朋友’我待他们不坏，应该不至于没良心。”当铺朝奉都出在徽州，所以胡雪岩称之为“徽州朋友”。古应春听他这一番话，便知他对自己的典当的积弊，一无所知，同时也觉得自己的看法，对胡雪岩确实有用。
en: Hu's face alternately flushed and paled. Despite the late-autumn weather, sweat dampened his back. “I knew nothing of this, Seventh Sister. When I return, I shall investigate and give the culprit a thorough dressing-down.” “There is no need. The man no longer works for you. That is why I have spoken.” “Then there are still others like him there?” She was silent, which amounted to assent. Since matters had reached this point, Gu decided to add his own counsel. He had followed Hu for years and knew much of the difficulty of establishing the business; his advice was therefore both extensive and penetrating. “You regard your pawnshops as a service to the poor, Little Uncle, and say you do not want to make money from them. But what pawnshop in the world makes no money? Because you have expressed that intention, even profits that ought properly to be earned are not appearing. Have you considered that?” “I have. I told them that a bank is a rich man's pawnshop, and a pawnshop is a poor man's bank. I deal with the rich. They pledge their credit or their connections; I can generally judge whether to accept the pledge and how much it is worth. There are too many poor people for me to look after personally, so I entrust them to the staff, who must act according to conscience. I have treated those Huizhou friends well. Surely they cannot be entirely without conscience.” Pawnshop appraisers came from Huizhou, hence his name for them. Gu realized from this speech that Hu knew nothing of the accumulated abuses in his own pawnshops. He also saw that his own observations could be of real use.

zh: “小爷叔，你有多少爿典当，你自己知道不知道？”胡雪岩一愣，搔搔头说：“二十家总有吧？”“小爷叔，”七姑奶奶怂恿着说：“你倒算算看！从杭州算起。”从杭州算起，首先便是公济，这是胡雪岩所设的第一家当铺，然后是广顺，武林门外拱震桥，运河起点，专为方便漕帮的泰安，浙江的杭州、胡州、嘉兴、海宁、金华、衢州、江苏的苏州，镇江，还有湖北。湖南，一共二十三家。当铺的资本，称为“架本”，向例不用银数，而以钱数计算，一千文准银一两，一万银子便称为一万千文。典当有大有小，架本少则五万千文，大则二十万千文，通扯以十万计，二十三家典当的架本。便是两百三十万银子，如果以“架货”折价，至少要加一倍。“小爷叔，架本总共算它四百五十万银子好了，做生意打它一分息，算低了吧，一个月就是四万五千银子，怎么样用也用不完，小爷叔叫我别样生意都不必做，光是经营这二十三家典当好了。”胡雪岩心想一个月四万五，一年就是五十四万，在他记忆中，每年年底结总帐，典当部分的盈余，从未超过二十万，照此说来，每年有三十多万银子，为“徽州朋友”吞掉了。
en: “Do you know how many pawnshops you own, Little Uncle?” Hu was taken aback. Scratching his head, he said, “There must be twenty?” “Count them,” the Seventh Lady urged. “Start with Hangzhou.” First came Gongji, the earliest shop Hu had established; then Guangshun and Tai'an, at Gongzhen Bridge outside Wulin Gate, the starting point of the canal, set up especially for the convenience of the grain-transport brotherhood. Across Hangzhou, Huzhou, Jiaxing, Haining, Jinhua, and Quzhou in Zhejiang, Suzhou and Zhenjiang in Jiangsu, and Hubei and Hunan, there were twenty-three in all. A pawnshop's operating capital was called its shelf capital. By convention it was stated in copper cash rather than silver, at one thousand cash to a tael: ten thousand taels thus became ten thousand strings of a thousand cash. Shops varied in size, with shelf capital ranging from fifty thousand to two hundred thousand such strings. At an average of one hundred thousand each, the twenty-three shops represented 2,300,000 taels. If their pledged goods were valued instead, the figure would at least double. “Let us put the total at four and a half million taels,” Gu said. “A return of one per cent is a low estimate for a business like this. That would mean forty-five thousand taels a month—more than one could spend. You could have me give up all my other work and concentrate on managing these twenty-three pawnshops.” Hu calculated: forty-five thousand a month meant 540,000 a year. Yet he could not remember annual pawnshop profits ever exceeding two hundred thousand. On that reasoning, the Huizhou friends were swallowing more than three hundred thousand taels a year.

zh: “我一个月的开销，连应酬通通算在内，也不过四五万银子。典当弄好了，我可以立于不败之地。”胡雪岩问道：“应春，你看我应该从哪里下手来整顿？”“自然是从盘查着手。”“查了一家再查一家呢？还是一声号令一起查？”“自然是一起查。”“你是不是在信口开河？”七姑奶奶插嘴说道：“二十三家典当一起查，人手呢？不光是查帐，还要查架子上的货，不是外行做得了的。”“七姐，”胡雪岩拦住她的话说：“应春出这个主意，当然有他的诀窍。”“小爷叔说得对！”古应春得意他说：“我有个诀窍，不但快，而且切实，兼且还不会得罪人。这话怎么说呢？譬如一家一家查，当然就要从靠不住的那几家先下手，为的是叫他措手不及。但这一来，查出毛病来不必说，倘或倒是干干净净的，人家心里就会不舒服，以后就不容易得力了。”
en: “My monthly expenditure, including all entertaining, is only forty or fifty thousand taels. If the pawnshops were properly managed, I could put myself beyond defeat. Where do you think I should begin reforming them, Yingchun?” “Naturally, with an audit and inspection.” “One shop after another, or all together at a single order?” “All together, of course.” “Are you talking without thinking?” the Seventh Lady interrupted. “Where will you find enough people to inspect twenty-three shops at once? It is not merely checking accounts. The pledged goods on the shelves must be examined too, and outsiders cannot do that.” “Seventh Sister,” Hu stopped her, “if Yingchun proposes it, he must have a method.” “Exactly!” Gu answered with satisfaction. “My method is quick, thorough, and unlikely to offend anyone. Consider: if we inspect one shop after another, we naturally start with those we distrust, taking them by surprise. If faults appear, well and good. But if a shop proves entirely sound, its people will resent the suspicion, and it will be harder to obtain their best service afterwards.”

zh: “闲话少说。”七姑奶奶性急，“你既然有诀窍，赶快说啊！”“这个诀窍，不着痕迹，小爷叔，我劝你来个大扳位，二十三家的。管总，、‘管包’，通通调动，调动要办移交，接手的有责任，自然不敢马虎，这一来帐目、架货的虚实，不就都盘查清楚了？”“这个法子倒真巧妙。不过以小调大，没有话说，以大调小，难免会有闲话。”“这也有个法子。典当大小，拿它分成三等，同等的抽签互换，好坏相差有限，各凭运气，大家也就没话说了。”“再说，”七姑奶奶有补充的意见：“真正几个得力、做得好的，小爷叔不妨私下安慰奖赏他们。”“说得是，我回杭州就办。”
en: “Enough preliminaries!” the Seventh Lady said impatiently. “If you have a method, tell us.” “It leaves no sign of suspicion. Little Uncle, make a general reshuffle. Transfer all the managers and custodians of pledged goods among the twenty-three shops. Transfers require formal handovers, and each person taking over becomes responsible. Naturally, he will not dare be careless. In this way, both the accounts and the actual goods on the shelves will be thoroughly checked.” “That is ingenious. But moving a man from a small shop to a large one will cause no complaint; moving him from a large one to a small one certainly may.” “There is a remedy. Divide the shops into three classes according to size, and have those within each class draw lots for exchanges. The differences will be limited, and everyone will depend on his luck, leaving little ground for complaint.” “Besides,” the Seventh Lady added, “you can privately reassure and reward the few who are truly capable and have done well.” “Quite right. I shall arrange it when I return to Hangzhou.”
